newsitem.title: USA: Hudson Foods plans $18 mln expansion.
newsitem.headline: Hudson Foods plans $18 mln expansion.

text.p: Hudson Foods Inc said on Wednesday that it planned to invest $18 million to expand its poultry-processing plant in Corydon, Ind., in a move that would create 200 jobs and increase production to 650,000 chickens per week.
The expansion is expected to be completed by April 1.

Hudson said the expansion will include 55,000 square feet of additional processing area, a 1.5 million pound holding freezer, an upgrade to the company's current wastewater pretreatment facility and a new office complex.

Hudson said the Corydon facility recently began a night shift that increased its capacity to 475,000 chickens per week, up from 350,000. It said the company already hired 80 employees out of the 200 new workers to handle the new shift.
The expansion also will create a need for more contract growers in the area, said Arkansas-based Hudson, which processes meat as well as poultry.
"We need to build an additional 35 to 40 chicken houses for us to reach our new capacity of 650,000 chickens," Kevin Burch, live production manager for Hudson's Corydon complex, said in a statement.
